recipes.title: Paneer Tikka (Air Fryer, Oven or Pan)
recipes.description: Smoky, tangy paneer and vegetable skewers in a hung-curd tandoori marinade. Kept keto-friendly by going light on onion and using thick hung curd.

steps.title: Measure everything
steps.text: Set out the paneer, capsicum, onion, hung curd and all the spices. Measuring first keeps the marinade balanced.
steps.visual: A whole block of paneer, one green capsicum and half an onion on a wooden board, beside a steel bowl of thick white hung curd and small steel katoris of red chilli powder, turmeric, tandoori masala, kasuri methi, ginger-garlic paste, half a lemon, a little mustard oil and salt

steps.title: Cut paneer and vegetables
steps.text: Cut the paneer into 1½-inch cubes. Cut the capsicum into squares of the same size and separate the onion into petals so everything cooks evenly.
steps.visual: Paneer cut into neat even cubes, capsicum squares and onion petals arranged in three piles on the wooden board, knife resting beside them

steps.title: Mix the marinade
steps.text: In a large bowl whisk the hung curd with ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli, turmeric, tandoori masala, crushed kasuri methi, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt until smooth and thick.
steps.visual: A wide steel mixing bowl holding a thick, smooth, deep orange-red yoghurt marinade being stirred with a spoon; empty spice katoris pushed to the side

steps.title: Coat the paneer
steps.text: Add the paneer cubes, capsicum and onion to the marinade. Fold gently with your hands or a spatula so every piece is coated without breaking the paneer.
steps.visual: Paneer cubes, capsicum squares and onion petals fully coated in the orange-red marinade inside the same steel bowl

steps.title: Rest to marinate
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it in the fridge for at least 30 minutes so the flavours soak in. You can marinate up to 8 hours ahead.
steps.visual: The same steel bowl of coated paneer and vegetables covered with a plate, sitting on a fridge shelf

steps.title: Thread the skewers
steps.text: Thread paneer, capsicum and onion alternately onto skewers. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 10 minutes first so they don't burn.
steps.visual: Four skewers threaded with alternating marinated paneer cubes, capsicum squares and onion petals laid on a tray, the empty marinade bowl behind

steps.title: Cook until charred
steps.text: Air fry at 200°C for 12 minutes, turning halfway, until the edges char. In an oven, grill at 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes. On a pan, cook over medium-high heat with a few drops of oil, turning every 2 minutes.
steps.visual: Paneer tikka skewers inside an open air-fryer basket, edges lightly charred and blistered, marinade turned deep red-brown

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala over the hot tikka and serve straight away with a squeeze of lemon. Pair with a cucumber salad to keep the meal low-carb.
steps.visual: Charred paneer tikka with capsicum and onion pushed off the skewers onto a white plate, dusted with chaat masala, a lemon wedge on the side

substitutions.note: Use firm tofu, pressed dry, to make it vegan; swap hung curd for thick coconut yoghurt.
Any neutral oil works; mustard oil just adds the classic pungency.
Strain regular curd in a muslin cloth for 2 hours — wet curd makes the marinade slide off.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate cooked tikka in an airtight box for up to 2 days. Raw marinated paneer keeps 24 hours in the fridge.
recipes.reheating: Reheat in the air fryer at 180°C for 3 minutes or on a hot pan; microwaving makes paneer rubbery.

recipes.title: Kottayam Fish Curry with Kudampuli
recipes.description: Kerala's fiery red fish curry, soured with kudampuli and finished in coconut oil — no coconut milk, naturally low in carbs, and even better the next day.

ingredients.prep: soaked in ½ cup warm water

steps.title: Soak the kudampuli
steps.text: Rinse the kudampuli and soak it in half a cup of warm water for 10 minutes. Keep the soaking water — it carries the sourness.
steps.visual: Two dark, leathery pieces of kudampuli soaking in a small steel bowl of warm water on a granite counter

steps.title: Prepare the fish and aromatics
steps.text: Wash the fish steaks and pat them dry. Slice the shallots and garlic, julienne the ginger and slit the green chillies.
steps.visual: Clean seer-fish steaks on a plate next to sliced shallots, garlic slivers, ginger matchsticks and slit green chillies on a wooden board

steps.title: Make the chilli paste
steps.text: Mix the Kashmiri chilli powder, chilli powder and turmeric with 3 tablespoons of water into a thick, smooth paste.
steps.visual: A small bowl of thick, glossy brick-red chilli and turmeric paste with a spoon resting in it

steps.title: Temper in coconut oil
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai or clay pot over medium heat. Add mustard seeds; when they splutter add fenugreek seeds and curry leaves for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds popping in shimmering coconut oil in a black kadai, curry leaves crackling and a few fenugreek seeds turning golden

steps.title: Sauté the aromatics
steps.text: Add the shallots, ginger, garlic and green chillies. Sauté for 4 to 5 minutes until the shallots turn soft and golden.
steps.visual: Golden, softened shallots with ginger, garlic and green chillies sizzling among curry leaves in the same black kadai

steps.title: Cook the chilli paste
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the chilli paste and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until the raw smell goes and oil starts to separate at the edges.
steps.visual: Deep red masala in the kadai with coconut oil glistening at the edges, shallots coated in the paste

steps.title: Add water and kudampuli
steps.text: Pour in the water along with the kudampuli and its soaking water. Add salt and bring to a gentle boil.
steps.visual: Thin, bright red curry gently bubbling in the kadai with dark kudampuli pieces floating in it

steps.title: Simmer the fish
steps.text: Slide in the fish steaks in a single layer. Don't stir — swirl the pot instead so the fish stays whole. Simmer on low for 10 to 12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the curry thickens.
steps.visual: Seer-fish steaks submerged in a thickened red curry in the kadai, coconut oil pooling on top, curry leaves scattered

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Turn off the heat and let the curry rest for at least 15 minutes before serving. Serve with matta rice for a balanced meal, or with cauliflower rice to keep it low-carb.
steps.visual: Kottayam fish curry served in a traditional clay pot, glossy red gravy with fish steaks and curry leaves, a banana leaf beneath

substitutions.note: Mackerel or sardines are cheaper and richer in omega-3; reduce simmering to 8 minutes.
Use a small lemon-sized ball of tamarind if kudampuli isn't available — it adds a few more carbs.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the flavour deepens overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat without stirring until just simmering.

recipes.title: Chettinad Chicken Pepper Fry
recipes.description: Dry, peppery chicken from Tamil Nadu's Chettinad region, roasted with freshly crushed black pepper, fennel and curry leaves.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Wash and drain the chicken. Rub it with curd, turmeric and half the salt and set aside for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Bone-in chicken pieces in a steel bowl coated in a thin layer of curd and turmeric, a pinch of salt on top

steps.title: Crush the pepper masala
steps.text: Dry roast the black pepper, fennel and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant, then coarsely crush them in a mixer or mortar — not to a fine powder.
steps.visual: Coarsely crushed black pepper, fennel and cumin in a stone mortar, a few whole peppercorns still visible

steps.title: Sauté shallots and curry leaves
steps.text: Heat sesame oil in a heavy kadai. Add cinnamon and curry leaves, then the shallots and green chillies. Sauté until the shallots are golden, about 5 minutes.
steps.visual: Golden sliced shallots, slit green chillies and crackling curry leaves with a piece of cinnamon in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic and tomato
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then add the tomato, chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook until the tomato breaks down into a thick masala.
steps.visual: Thick reddish-brown masala with softened tomato and shallots in the iron kadai, oil glistening at the edges

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and the remaining salt. Toss well, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then. The chicken releases its own juices — add a splash of water only if it sticks.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces coated in the masala, simmering in their own juices in the covered iron kadai with the lid slightly ajar

steps.title: Roast with pepper
steps.text: Uncover, add the crushed pepper masala and roast on medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is dry, dark and coated.
steps.visual: Dark, dry-roasted chicken pieces flecked with coarse black pepper and curry leaves in the iron kadai

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Scatter chopped coriander over the pepper chicken and serve hot with a vegetable poriyal and a small portion of rice, or with cucumber raita for a low-carb plate.
steps.visual: Chettinad pepper chicken heaped in a brass bowl, garnished with fresh coriander and fried curry leaves, a banana leaf and a cabbage poriyal beside it

substitutions.note: Boneless thigh cooks faster (10 minutes covered) and has no bone weight.
Coconut oil gives a Kerala-style finish.
Use lemon juice for a dairy-free marinade.

recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan over medium heat with a teaspoon of water.

recipes.title: Coconut Cauliflower Rice
recipes.description: A South Indian–style tempered cauliflower 'rice' with coconut, curry leaves and cashew — a light, low-carb base for sambar, fish curry or chicken fry.

steps.title: Rice the cauliflower
steps.text: Pulse the cauliflower florets in a mixer jar in short bursts until they look like grains of rice. Don't over-blend into a paste. You can also grate them on a box grater.
steps.visual: Cauliflower florets in a mixer jar beside a steel plate of freshly riced cauliflower that looks like rice grains

steps.title: Temper the spices
steps.text: Heat coconut oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds; once they splutter add urad dal and cashews and fry until golden, then add curry leaves, green chilli and ginger.
steps.visual: Golden urad dal and cashews with spluttering mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and chopped ginger in coconut oil in a kadai

steps.title: Stir-fry the cauliflower
steps.text: Add the riced cauliflower and salt. Stir-fry on medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes without covering, so it stays fluffy rather than mushy.
steps.visual: Riced cauliflower tossed with the tempering in the kadai, turning slightly translucent, flecks of mustard and curry leaves throughout

steps.title: Add coconut and lemon
steps.text: Turn off the heat, fold in the grated coconut and squeeze over the lemon juice.
steps.visual: Fresh white grated coconut being folded into the cauliflower rice in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as a rice replacement with sambar, fish curry or pepper chicken.
steps.visual: Fluffy coconut cauliflower rice in a steel bowl with golden cashews and curry leaves on top, a small bowl of fish curry beside it

substitutions.note: Peanuts are cheaper and similar in carbs; skip both for a nut-free version.

recipes.storage: Best fresh. Raw riced cauliflower keeps 2 days refrigerated.
recipes.reheating: Stir-fry for 1 minute in a hot pan.
